domain: Looks up the current battle-effect resource entry, spawns a linked effect object offset above it, clears and re-masks two visual flag bytes, loads a VRAM block keyed by a visual byte, optionally installs the EmitRandomParticleEffect callback and an extra dispatch call from the flags argument, then waits and releases the object.
notes: Adapted from the family template (080937b8, spawn_linked_resource_object.c): same struct roles (resource x/y/z at +8/+12/+16, object visual pointer at +0x50, object callback at +0x6c reused from the template's exact BattleEffectLinkedObject layout), but this owner spawns kind 0x16 (not 0x15) at y+0x240000, reads a byte field at visual+0x1c (not the template's +0x26) for a VramBlock_LoadCached(Func_08003fa4) call, and clears two extra visual bytes at +0x26/+0x27 that the template does not touch.

Correcting the visual byte-field offset from an initial (wrong) 0x28 guess to the true 0x1c collapsed the candidate from a multi-instruction pointer-arithmetic load to the reference's single ldrb with immediate offset -- worth 14 differing halfwords by itself.

The only remaining residual is a single instruction at the first flags-byte mask: the reference computes the AND mask for `flags_a &= ~0x20` via `subs r3, #33` (reusing the r3 register that still held the constant 0 from the two preceding byte-clear stores), while every ordinary-C spelling tried here (`&= ~0x20` directly, an explicit `mask = 33; mask = -mask;` runtime-negate matching the template's own idiom for the second flags byte, and an explicit `zero` local reused across the stores and the mask) instead produces either the semantically-identical 8-bit-truncated `movs r3, #223` (1-for-1 same size, wrong encoding) or a longer 2-instruction negate (`movs`+`negs`, +4 bytes, further from reference). The second flags-byte mask (`(flags_b & 0x0f) & ~0x0c) | 4`, written as an explicit `s32 clear = 13; clear = -clear;` local exactly matching the template's negate idiom) reproduces the reference byte-for-byte, including its own `negs` instruction and register roles.

This is a single-instruction constant-materialization choice (reuse of a live zero register vs. a fresh immediate load), the same class of residual documented for 08095c08 (register/CSE scheduling, not source shape); a few bounded respellings did not reproduce it and further search was not pursued given the reward is a single halfword out of 204 bytes.

Recovered only from retained GS1 assembly, the local exact-C BattleEffectLinkedObject/VramBlock_LoadCached/ObjectTable_Get declarations already established by other owners, and the approved compiler. No GS2 evidence or external source was used.
